summary: The mechanism is sound. The cumulative-offset premise is TRUE (CommitLog.recover() then open()->crossFrom() leaves nextOffsets cumulative before CheckpointWriter is ever constructed, so the induction holds), the I3 barrier S-1<=upTo is exactly right (a checkpoint at S covers [0,S-1]; applyChain applies [0,upTo] inclusive), seeding nextSequence only on the own epoch mirrors applyChain's own ownEpoch gate and is correct, and startAfter=keyFor(from-1) is guarded at from==0, needs no existing key under the BinStore.list contract, pages correctly and sits before every ckpt/ key so M4.8b1's filter is unaffected. No request rate scales with records, shards, partitions or indices, and an unbounded ancestry still terminates on the strictly-decreasing-epoch check. Three findings: the file now contains a MUST NOT that this commit violates and leaves uncorrected; the cost budget in the one test that pins takeover request rate is relaxed for the second time without the ADR cost.md R18 mandates, on a row whose whole purpose was to redeem the first relaxation; and the neverOpened arithmetic branch adds hops without probing, leaving one full-chain replay outside the bound.

findings.title: newestCheckpoint's javadoc still says "M4.9 MUST NOT CALL IT WITH ITS OWN" epoch, which is exactly what line 129 now does
findings.detail: Lines 361-367 read: 'IT ANSWERS FOR ONE EPOCH, the one passed, and M4.9 MUST NOT CALL IT WITH ITS OWN. A leader acquires a FRESH epoch ... so its own chain is empty at the moment it recovers and this returns EMPTY at every takeover. The checkpoints that bound the replay are the PREDECESSOR's, reached through firstInheritableAncestor.' This commit's replayAncestry (line 129) calls crossFromCheckpoint(hops, epoch, upTo) with the own epoch as the first hop, and reaches the predecessor through the CONTINUE walk rather than through firstInheritableAncestor. Lines 123-128 argue the opposite of lines 361-367 in the same file, twenty lines apart, and neither note mentions the other. Lines 377-383 are stale in the same way -- 'M4.9 needs a bound on the WALK, not only on the replay' is written as an open requirement in a file where M4.9 has landed. This project's own convention, visible in a dozen places in this same class ("an earlier draft claimed ... that was measured FALSE"), is to correct a superseded note in the commit that supersedes it.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer touching newestCheckpoint reads the MUST NOT, sees the plausible supporting reason ('returns EMPTY at every takeover'), and deletes the first-hop probe at line 129 as a wasted stat -- the same request the author of this commit removed one round of the failover-cost budget to pay for. inherited() is the crossing that actually reads the ancestry and it STARTS at the predecessor, so with the first-hop probe gone the bound does nothing on the only path that matters and per-failover cost silently returns to O(all commit-log entries ever written). More immediately: the file contains two contradictory directives about the same call and a reader has no way to tell which one this commit decided.
findings.remedy: Rewrite the newestCheckpoint javadoc so it records what M4.9 actually decided -- every chain on the walk is probed once, including the first hop, because inherited() enters at the predecessor -- and retire or restate the 'M4.9 owns the difference' paragraph now that it does.

findings.title: The takeover request-rate budget is relaxed a second time with no ADR, on the very row that was the promissory note for the first relaxation
findings.detail: The per-epoch checkpoint probe (line 129 and line 162) adds one stat per takeover plus one per ancestor, and LocalSequencerFailoverTest.aTakeoverReadsEveryEntryOfEveryANCESTORAndTHATISAREGRESSION's totals move up accordingly: 28->30 (:195), 56->58 (:198), 20->22 (:208), 47->52 (:219). cost.md R18 is explicit -- 'Never relax a budget to make a check pass. Moving a budget is an ADR with the number, the rejected alternative, and what the new budget buys' -- and non-negotiable 2 repeats it. What is staged is a code comment and a backlog-done paragraph. The backlog row gives the number and what it buys but names no rejected alternative, no ADR is added or amended (ADR-0034 costs discovery per epoch but records no budget move), and no baselines/review.txt entry is staged. This is not the ordinary case of an undisclosed move: M4.9's own notes at HEAD state that M4.6e relaxed THESE FOUR ASSERTIONS and that 'this row IS the evidence carrying a non-negotiable-2 exception', i.e. the exception was granted against M4.9 making the claim true. M4.9 lands and moves the same four numbers further up, and the test's new comment concedes 'THE SHAPE IS UNCHANGED ... cost still grows per ancestor and per entry', while the older comment two paragraphs above it -- left unedited at :144 -- still asserts 'M4.8's checkpoints are what make this constant again'. Both sentences are now in the same comment block and they contradict each other.
findings.failure_scenario: The one test in the tree that pins takeover request rate has now been relaxed twice, each time on the strength of a future backlog row, and the second relaxation is the redemption of the first. The next author facing the same test has identical precedent and no ADR stating what the budget is, what it bought, or which alternative was rejected -- so the third move is cheaper than the second, and the budget ratchets upward with the reasoning living only in commit-adjacent prose. Concretely: nothing in the tree now records that skipping the own-epoch probe was considered and rejected, so the same +1-per-takeover will be re-litigated or re-paid the next time this path is touched.
findings.remedy: Either write the ADR R18 asks for (the four numbers, the rejected alternative -- gating the first-hop probe on epoch != ownEpoch, which would have cost the restart-recovering-its-own-chain shape the new test pins -- and what the move buys), or stage a baselines/review.txt entry arguing that the backlog row is sufficient. Either way correct the now-false 'M4.8's checkpoints are what make this constant again' sentence at LocalSequencerFailoverTest.java:144, which this commit disproves.

findings.title: The neverOpened arithmetic branch adds a hop with from=0 and never probes it, so one full chain escapes the bound
findings.detail: In the CONTINUE branch the target chainEpoch is probed (line 162) before its hop is added, so every chain reached by following a CONTINUE is bounded. In the neverOpened branch (lines 186-191) chainEpoch is decremented and hops.add(new Hop(chainEpoch, 0, limit)) runs with no crossFromCheckpoint call at all; the next loop iteration probes that chain's PREDECESSOR, not the chain itself. A run of burned epochs therefore delivers the first genuinely-opened ancestor with from=0 and upTo=Long.MAX_VALUE, and it is replayed entry by entry even though its checkpoint pointer would have terminated the walk at once.
findings.failure_scenario: CommitLog.recover() on an epoch E whose chain carries a Seal at slot 0 -- a leader that acquired E and died before writing its CONTINUE, then fenced by a successor -- walks by arithmetic to E-1 and replays E-1 in full: one LIST per 1000 keys plus one GET per entry of a term that may hold a million deltas, with E-1's checkpoint sitting unread at a known key. It is unreachable on today's takeover path only because LocalSequencer.start resolves burned epochs through firstInheritableAncestor before inherited() is ever called -- an ordering invariant held in another class, which is precisely the class of caveat neverOpened's own javadoc (lines 267-279) records rather than assumes.
findings.remedy: Probe in the arithmetic branch too, symmetrically with the CONTINUE branch: if (chainEpoch >= 1 && crossFromCheckpoint(hops, chainEpoch, limit)) { atOrigin = false; break; } before the hops.add. If it is deliberately left open, record it here the way the neverOpened caveat is recorded.
